title: Differentials of a finitely presented commutative algebra are finitely presented
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Suppose that $A$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra, meaning that $A\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ as an $R$-algebra for some finite $m,n$ and polynomials $g_j$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then the module of Kahler differentials $\Omega_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a finitely presented $A$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]: there are finite $u,v$ and an exact sequence $A^u\to A^v\to\Omega_{A/R}\to0$. No Noetherian or flatness hypothesis is imposed.
